title: Multi-level Memory-Centric Profiling on ARM Processors with ARM SPE
problem: ARM processors lack specialized memory-centric profiling tools comparable to Intel PEBS and AMD IBS for x86 processors. Characterizing how ARM's Statistical Profiling Extension performs for accurate memory profiling on HPC and cloud systems is an open problem.
motivation: As ARM processors increasingly deploy in HPC and data center environments, efficient memory profiling is essential for identifying bottlenecks and guiding optimizations.
method: The authors develop a memory profiling tool using ARM's Statistical Profiling Extension (SPE, a hardware feature that periodically records memory accesses without stopping the processor by sampling events). They test the tool on ARM Ampere processors running HPC and cloud workloads. The evaluation measures two key metrics: execution overhead (how much profiling slows the system down) and sampling accuracy (whether sampled memory accesses represent actual behavior), across different sampling intervals and buffer configurations.
key_novelty: This paper provides the first measurements of ARM SPE's execution overhead and sampling accuracy for memory profiling at multiple system levels, establishing its feasibility for production HPC systems.
contributions: Multi-level memory profiling tool specifically designed for ARM processors
Systematic evaluation of ARM SPE capabilities and limitations for memory-centric profiling
Quantitative assessment of ARM SPE time overhead and sampling accuracy at varying configurations
Comparative analysis across both HPC and Cloud workloads
